title: Keep residual parameter normalization finite in half precision
tests: 1 failed, 18 passed before; 273 passed, 6 skipped after excluding Gloo module
novelty: 13 reachable historical mlp.py blobs, a single normalize_parameters variant; none promote low-precision weight normalization
head: ced6972321fff833ff631aa65629988f91031999
body:
## Problem

`ResidualMLP.normalize_parameters()` computes parameter norms in the parameter dtype. With finite FP16 weights of 20000 and batch-normalization biases of 10000, the squared norm overflows, so normalization replaces a nonzero direction with zeros. Zero rows in linear weights also encounter an epsilon that underflows in half precision. This affects the parameter projection performed after optimizer steps for residual SAC models.

## Change

Compute linear, batch-normalization and RMS parameter normalization in at least float32, then copy the normalized values back into the original parameters. Float32/float64 precision and the parameter dtype are retained.

## Validation

- Regression uses a real `ResidualMLP` with linear, batch-normalization and RMS weights; checks FP16/FP32/FP64 parameters against a float64 reference and verifies finite forward inference.
- Unchanged implementation: **1 failed, 18 passed** in the focused model tests. Fixed independent branch: **273 passed, 6 skipped** in the local suite excluding the Gloo module.
- Combined fork integration with the metric-snapshot and collection fixes: **284 passed, 6 skipped** on Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12, including existing real two-process Gloo tests. Lint and Docs also pass. [Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43894272107).
- All repository pre-commit hooks pass.

This changes post-update parameter projection. The separate ONNX forward RMS normalization fix in #286 addresses another execution path.

title: Snapshot episode metrics before environment buffers are reused
tests: 2 failed, 4 passed before; 272 passed, 6 skipped after excluding Gloo module
novelty: 55 reachable historical logger.py blobs, 8 process_env_step variants, all retain environment mapping references; #267 changes aggregation only
head: 14d1797ff5d70c58e3e43874df2459f64b99ef63
body:
## Problem

`Logger.process_env_step()` queues the environment's metric dictionary directly. If the environment reuses that dictionary or updates its tensor buffers before the next log flush, earlier episode samples change as well. For successive reward samples `[1, 3]` and `[9, 9]`, the reported mean becomes 9 instead of 5.5. Mutable scalar entries in a reused dictionary are affected too.

## Change

Snapshot the selected `episode`/`log` mapping when collecting it and detach/clone its tensor values. Preserve the existing preference for `episode` when both keys are present. This keeps the stored samples independent of later environment mutations and avoids retaining their autograd graphs.

## Validation

- Reuse both dictionary and tensor buffers under each supported key; mutate them between collection calls and verify the eventual logged means, original snapshot, detached tensors and environment-owned values.
- Unchanged implementation: **2 failed, 4 passed** in the logger tests. Fixed independent branch: **272 passed, 6 skipped** in the local suite excluding the Gloo module.
- Combined fork integration with residual parameter normalization and collection fixes: **284 passed, 6 skipped** on Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12, including existing real two-process Gloo tests. Lint and Docs also pass. [Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43894272107).
- All repository pre-commit hooks pass.

Related: #267 changes aggregation at log flush. This patch fixes ownership at collection time; aggregation cannot recover samples that were already overwritten.

title: Keep recurrent rollout collection outside autograd graphs
tests: 4 failed, 43 passed before; 274 passed, 6 skipped after excluding Gloo module
novelty: 118 historical PPO blobs and 53 Distillation blobs, 12/5 act variants; none disable gradients during direct collection
head: d80408e5c32f54be094c366007767e0666de47bc
body:
## Problem

Direct use of `PPO.act()` or `Distillation.act()` outside the runner's `inference_mode` context records recurrent sampling graphs. Detaching returned actions does not detach the recurrent hidden state. In PPO, those graphs enter saved rollout states and a second learning epoch raises `Trying to backward through the graph a second time`. Distillation also keeps unnecessary teacher-state graphs during direct collection.

## Change

Run both public collection methods under `torch.no_grad()`, matching SAC collection and the runner's existing intended separation between sampling and learning. Gradient-enabled model calls in the update methods remain available for training.

## Validation

- GRU and LSTM direct PPO collection followed by two real learning epochs; verify finite losses, detached rollout states and changed model parameters.
- GRU and LSTM direct distillation collection followed by a real student update; verify detached teacher states and changed student parameters.
- Unchanged implementation: **4 failed, 43 passed** in the focused algorithm tests. Fixed independent branch: **274 passed, 6 skipped** in the local suite excluding the Gloo module.
- Combined fork integration with the normalization and metric-snapshot fixes: **284 passed, 6 skipped** on Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12, including existing real two-process Gloo tests. Lint and Docs also pass. [Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43894272107).
- All repository pre-commit hooks pass.
